answer: Rising ticket price curve: identity N costs base × (1 + N/1,000), so mass registration climbs a price schedule, not a gate. Payment uses marble credits; each ticket’s price is set from the identity count, so an attacker pays a rising per-identity amount. Each ticket also needs a fresh signature from a ferrous hardware module, blocking cheap virtual copies. The module releases one pulse per interval, so extra identities require more modules and waiting out the schedule.
